title: Prove a Fibonacci paid-scan floor for two dense dirty outputs (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration: S distinct-bank monomial ADD scans and unary gates of total row-support exponent R can produce two banks of row support D only if `2^R F_(S+1)>=D`. This tracks the two largest bank support sizes and strengthens the inherited single-maximum estimate. Arbitrary finite restored dirty helpers and arbitrary per-bank monomial maps are allowed.

```text
before: one support maximum gives 2^(R+S) >= D
new:    two bank maxima give 2^R F_(S+1) >= D
L=3, R=0, two full chirps: necessary ADD count 3 -> 5
```

This takes the explicit constant-scan next question in Ross Richardson's merged #4023. His #4082 and #4057 retain the earlier support and paid-endpoint method credit. The new contribution is the two-bank invariant and its tradeoff, not a new general support-union or Fibonacci method. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Only `research/fibonacci-scan-floor/` is added; no selected-frontier change or new kappa is claimed.

## Evidence

`PASS_FIBONACCI_SCAN_FLOOR`: 315884 enumerated support-relaxation layer states, 2304 exact F5 matrix prefixes, dense chirp tensor rows through seven bits, and ten rejection controls. Two algorithms corroborate the written induction; no predecessor executable is replayed. A generated complete receipt binds all mathematical fields to proof, code and metadata hashes. Boolean receipt changes, proof-byte drift and occupied receipt output reject; Git-free optimized replay passes.

Run from the repository root with CPython 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fibonacci-scan-floor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/fibonacci-scan-floor --check-source-history
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/fibonacci-scan-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/fibonacci-scan-floor/verify.py
```

Other machines may substitute their CPython 3.12 path. Both registered commands pass locally in 0.530 and 0.527 seconds on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64. Metadata/provenance, exact committed bytes/source history and official export checks pass at `1c98c7261ccb03e089c61f006c29ba0a47d3f42f`.

## Limitations

The count is a serial full-bank ADD count with distinct source and destination banks. General free bank GL, same-bank buffered additions charged as ordinary scans, multi-bank native gates, partial volumes and fused traversals require different models. An explicit invertible F5 same-bank example demonstrates that boundary. R is a sum of supplied row-support exponents; actual native recipes must establish their own support laws. No matching scan optimum, complete physical supplier, precision/tape price, selected cold replay, formal proof-kernel or independent human review is claimed. All registered obligations ran locally; full supplier and formal proof obligations remain outside scope.

## Open next questions

- Determine the exact inter-bank ADD optimum between this bound and #4023's cited six-per-bit construction. Start at one bit with explicit coefficients and two banks; no matching construction is supplied here.
- Derive a weighted support bound for a declared partial-volume or fused traversal model. Its row-update and movement tariff must be specified first.

## Related open work

- #4875 counts same-phase native C/C^-1 calls for three dirty source-to-target shears. This package counts monomial ADD scans for two complete chirps under a different alphabet; it does not recompute that PR's optimum.
- #4899 optimizes weighted borrowed-source tours for prescribed pair-parity targets. Its scalar row ADD count concerns a different endpoint and alphabet; no shared numerical quantity is computed here.

Live overlap covered 411 open PRs plus the refreshed recent-open list, latest handoff claims, all-main README searches and merged searches for the object, formula and Fibonacci terms. Sparse local note coverage and arbitrary diffs remain incomplete. No other open PR studying this exact two-bank chirp scan bound was found within that coverage. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19134252).
